title: Block the backdoor path without deleting the mechanism
description: Choose an adjustment set for a product-policy study. The graph and estimate reveal why confounders, mediators, and colliders cannot be treated as interchangeable features.

nodes.label: Product engagement
nodes.detail: Carries part of the policy effect.

nodes.label: Support contact
nodes.detail: Can be caused by both account risk and policy friction.

policies.label: Adjust for nothing
policies.detail: Compare exposed and unexposed accounts directly.
policies.explanation: Account maturity keeps a backdoor path open between policy exposure and retention.

policies.label: Adjust for account maturity
policies.detail: Block the common cause of treatment and outcome.
policies.explanation: The selected set blocks the backdoor path while leaving the engagement mechanism intact.

policies.label: Adjust for product engagement
policies.detail: Condition on a variable caused by the policy.
policies.explanation: Conditioning on the mediator removes part of the total effect the study intends to measure.

policies.label: Adjust for support contact
policies.detail: Condition on a shared consequence of policy friction and account risk.
policies.explanation: Selecting on support contact creates an association that was absent in the unconditioned population.

measurementPolicies.label: Reliable maturity measure
measurementPolicies.detail: Tenure and lifecycle fields represent the pre-treatment state.

measurementPolicies.label: Noisy maturity proxy
measurementPolicies.detail: A partial activity score weakly represents the confounder.

measurementPolicies.label: Post-treatment snapshot
measurementPolicies.detail: The field may already contain effects of the new policy.
